rubrics.justification: The response correctly identifies a very poor-quality early/poorly cavitating blastocyst with absent/degenerative ICM and TE, consistent with 0DD. Minor issues include some uncertainty about whether a blastocoel is present and wording that drifts toward 'non-blast/arrested embryo,' which goes slightly beyond the provided grading.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, diagnosis, semen parameters, endometrium, lifestyle, and first-cycle status well, and appropriately frames embryo morphology as the dominant prognostic factor despite favorable patient background.

The reasoning is structured and internally consistent, with conclusions generally supported by morphology and clinical context. Minor overreach appears in treating this single poor embryo as potentially 'more than just a single bad embryo event' after one cycle.

The interpretation is broadly aligned with Gardner grading and standard IVF counseling, including poor prognosis for 0DD and caution about PGT-A in a 32-year-old first cycle. Small deviations include some speculative checks (e.g., OHSS, progesterone) that are not central to this case.

Provides practical counseling, supports single embryo transfer if this is the only embryo, and outlines sensible future-cycle review steps. It is useful and specific, though some recommendations are somewhat broad rather than tightly prioritized.
